**Finding submitted: deviation (ASSIGN), fallback-level cure.**

- **Responsive clause:** Section 10 (NONASSIGNABILITY), p0042 — the only assignment provision in the document. Searches for "assign" and "change of control" confirmed no change-of-control mechanic anywhere, and Section 6 contains only mutual convenience/breach termination rights, so no Vendor exit or re-pricing on our change of control (walk-away trigger absent).
- **Why it fails fallback:** all assignments, including to a successor in a merger, acquisition or asset sale, require the other party's prior consent; the fallback requires a mutual successor right on written notice. The consent and "not unreasonably withheld" elements were already met verbatim.
- **Cure:** one inserted sentence adding the mutual successor carve-out on written notice, leaving the existing consent standard for all other assignments untouched (no affiliate exception, which would conflict with the fallback level).
